Question 9 of 11 · The Quran

Does the Quran contain knowledge ahead of its time?

Short answer

Revealed in the 7th century, it describes the embryo growing in stages and the universe expanding.

Source: Quran 23:12–14 (opens in a new tab) Quran 51:47 (opens in a new tab)

The evidence

1

The Quran describes the embryo developing in stages. What do you make of that?

“…then We developed the drop into a clinging clot, then developed the clot into a lump ˹of flesh˺, then developed the lump into bones, then clothed the bones with flesh…” — Quran 23:14

What the verses say

The verses describe a sequence: a drop, then a clinging clot, then a lump of flesh, then bones, then the bones clothed with flesh. They were recited in 7th-century Arabia. Read them in full and judge for yourself whether anyone then could have known this.

SourceQuran 23:12–14↗(opens in a new tab)

2

Embryology isn’t the only example.

The Quran also speaks of the universe expanding.

The expanding universe

وَالسَّمَاءَ بَنَيْنَاهَا بِأَيْدٍ وَإِنَّا لَمُوسِعُونَ

“We built the universe with ˹great˺ might, and We are certainly expanding ˹it˺.”

Quran 51:47

Today astronomers measure how fast the universe is expanding. They call the rate the Hubble constant.

SourceQuran 51:47↗(opens in a new tab)ArticleESA: Planck reveals an almost perfect Universe (2013)↗(opens in a new tab)

Objections

What people say against this, and our answer. Open one to read it.

You might say“Could it be a general description anyone might guess?”

Our answer

It's not a general description.

Why it's specific

The verses don’t just say that a baby grows. They name five stages in order: a drop, “a clinging clot,” “a lump ˹of flesh˺,” bones, and then bones “clothed … with flesh.”

SourceQuran 23:12–14↗(opens in a new tab)
You might say“He could have guessed or borrowed the knowledge”

Our answer

Could he have borrowed the knowledge?

Why borrowing doesn't explain it

People made this charge in his own lifetime, and the Quran answered it:

وَلَقَدْ نَعْلَمُ أَنَّهُمْ يَقُولُونَ إِنَّمَا يُعَلِّمُهُ بَشَرٌ ۗ لِّسَانُ الَّذِي يُلْحِدُونَ إِلَيْهِ أَعْجَمِيٌّ وَهَٰذَا لِسَانٌ عَرَبِيٌّ مُّبِينٌ

“And We surely know that they say, ‘No one is teaching him except a human.’ But the man they refer to speaks a foreign tongue, whereas this ˹Quran˺ is ˹in˺ eloquent Arabic.”

Quran 16:103
SourceQuran 16:103↗(opens in a new tab)

And he could not read, so he could not have copied from books (29:48).

SourceQuran 29:48↗(opens in a new tab)
You might say“Coincidences happen”

Our answer

Coincidence becomes increasingly unlikely.

The scale of the claim

One accurate statement could be a lucky guess. The question is whether a man in 7th-century Arabia could keep guessing right about things no one then could check. Look at the verses and decide for yourself.
